data.title: The Wind in the Willows · Chapter 1
data.text: The Mole had been working very hard all the morning, spring-cleaning his little home. First with brooms, then with dusters; then on ladders and steps and chairs, with a brush and a pail of whitewash; till he had dust in his throat and eyes, and splashes of whitewash all over his black fur, and an aching back and weary arms.
data.translation: 鼹鼠整个上午都在非常努力地干活，为他的小家做春季大扫除。先是拿着扫帚，然后拿着掸子；接着爬上梯子、台阶和椅子，拿着刷子和一桶石灰水；直到他的喉咙和眼睛里都是灰尘，黑色的皮毛上溅满了石灰水，后背酸痛，手臂疲惫不堪。

data.title: The Wind in the Willows · Chapter 2
data.text: Spring was moving in the air above and in the earth below and around him, penetrating even his dark and lowly little house with its spirit of divine discontent and longing. It was small wonder, then, that he suddenly flung down his brush on the floor, said 'Bother!' and 'O blow!' and also 'Hang spring-cleaning!' and bolted out of the house without even waiting to put on his coat.
data.translation: 春天在他上方的空气里、下方的土地里、以及周围的万物中流动，连他那阴暗低矮的小屋都被感染了那种神圣的不安与渴望。难怪他忽然把刷子扔到地上，骂了句"讨厌！""真该死！"还有"让春季大扫除见鬼去吧！"连外套都没来得及穿就冲出了家门。

data.title: The Wind in the Willows · Chapter 3
data.text: Something up above was calling him imperiously, and he made for the steep little tunnel which answered in his case to the galvanised iron and woodwork of the staircase. He scrambled up as best he could, dusting his paws off on the steps as he went, and finally, with a sigh of relief, found himself out in the open air. The mole felt that the call of the upper world was a call he could not refuse.
data.translation: 上方有什么东西在专横地呼唤他，他朝着那条陡峭的小隧道走去——那隧道对他来说就像楼梯的镀锌铁和木结构。他尽力向上爬，一边爬一边在台阶上蹭干净爪子，最后如释重负地叹了口气，终于来到开阔的天地间。鼹鼠觉得，上层世界的召唤是他无法拒绝的。
